title: Later faunas would outcompete earlier faunas under similar conditions

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Later faunas would outcompete earlier faunas under similar conditions

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because each new species arose by having some advantage over preceding forms, a more recent fauna or flora would beat and exterminate an older one if they were placed in competition under a similar climate, and in this sense recent forms are higher.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. X: On the Geological Succession of Organic Beings

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: If under a nearly similar climate, the eocene inhabitants of one quarter of the world were put into competition with the existing inhabitants of the same or some other quarter, the eocene fauna or flora would certainly be beaten and exterminated

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter X, “On the Geological Succession of Organic Beings”; section “On the state of development of ancient forms”. Scope: faunas and floras of successive geological periods

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch10-17: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.38

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The counterfactual can only be approached through proxies or models built from incomplete traits. Existing data can examine overlap and replacement in selected lineages but cannot resolve certain extermination of whole faunas.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Use reconstructed traits, niches, and food webs to simulate competition between matched Eocene and extant assemblages under the same climate, or test temporal replacement where older and newer lineages overlapped. Consistent estimated competitive dominance by recent forms would support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Most competitive traits and interactions do not fossilize.

Simulation results depend strongly on assumed mechanisms.

Direct competition between extinct and living communities cannot be observed.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.43
operationalizability: 0.43
data adequacy: 0.27
data existence: 0.5
discriminating power: 0.25

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The statement is a counterfactual about a meeting that the fossil record does not contain. Any real pattern of replacement is compatible with later forms being competitively superior and with later forms merely being different. Proxies require a substantial reinterpretation, so they do not resolve the claim as stated.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The stated test is a competition, under a similar climate, between an extinct fauna or flora and a living one. No existing observation records the winner of that encounter, and modern invasions or trait trends change the contrast into a different question.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Competitive superiority is not a variable stored in occurrence or trait data without replacing the claim.

Extinct species cannot be placed in competition with living ones.
